title: fsurf
summary: Plot scalar or parametric function surfaces.

gpu_support.notes: `fsurf` samples arbitrary function handles on the host, then uses RunMat's existing surface renderer. There is no provider kernel because MATLAB callbacks are not GPU kernels.

description: `fsurf` evaluates function handles over a rectangular two-variable domain and renders the sampled values as a 3-D surface. It supports ordinary `z = f(x,y)` surfaces and parametric surfaces supplied as `x = fx(u,v)`, `y = fy(u,v)`, and `z = fz(u,v)`.
behaviors: `fsurf(f, [xmin xmax ymin ymax])` uses an explicit rectangular domain; a two-element vector applies the same limits to both axes.
`fsurf(fx, fy, fz)` samples a parametric surface over the default parameter domain.
`fsurf(ax, ___)` renders into the requested axes and returns a function-surface graphics handle.
Function-handle outputs must be scalar real numeric values at every sampled point; non-finite explicit surface samples are preserved as surface discontinuities.
options: `'MeshDensity'` controls the number of samples along each domain dimension. RunMat accepts integer values from 2 through 400.
Surface style name/value pairs such as `'DisplayName'`, `'FaceAlpha'`, `'FaceColor'`, `'EdgeColor'`, `'Shading'`, `'Lighting'`, `'Visible'`, and `'Colormap'` use the same parsing path as `surf`.

faqs.question: Does `fsurf` evaluate the function handle on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB function handles can contain arbitrary user code, so RunMat samples them on the host and then hands the sampled surface to the plotting renderer.

faqs.question: What happens if the function returns a vector?
faqs.answer: RunMat raises `RunMat:fsurf:EvaluationFailed`; each sampled point must produce one scalar numeric value.

gpu_residency: `fsurf` is a callback-sampling builtin. It creates a new sampled surface and does not preserve input residency, because the inputs are MATLAB function handles rather than numeric provider buffers.
gpu_behavior: Callback sampling runs on the host.
The resulting surface uses the existing `runmat-plot` surface rendering path.
